I. INTRODUCTION 
As a non-invasive blood pressure (BP) measurement 
technique, the pulse transit time (PTT)-based method has the 
advantage of estimating t he blood pressure without cuff. 
However, it has a limitation that frequent calibration is 
required due to physiological changes of the arterial 
characteristics [1]. Therefore, it is necessary to eval uate the 
arterial characteristics in order to increase the availability of 
the PTT measurement method. In this study, we aimed to 
derive curve which might represent arterial characteristics 
through continuous BP and photoplethysmogram (PPG) and 
investigated changes inducing from forced blood pressure 
variation. 
II. METHODOLOGY 
The arterial distensibility (Da), which is one of indicators of 
arterial characteristic, is defined as the volume change 
according to the pressure applied to the blood vessel [2].

where V is blood volume and P is blood pressure. 
To derive distensibility -like curve with PPG and BP 
waveform, we obtained PPG and continuous BP (BPc) from 
volunteer’s left index finger and middle finger (23 years old, 
180.1 cm, 78.5 kg) , respectively. PPG was recorded with 
MP150 and OXY100E (Biopac Systems, inc., CA, USA), and 
BPc was recorded with Portapres (Finapres Medical Systems 
B.V, AMS, NED). The measurement was performed for 100 
seconds in supine position , and subject was asked to do 
Valsalva Maneuver (VM) for 15 seconds. Signal was 
obtained at 500 kHz sampling rate. BP and PPG were filtered 
 
 
with 2-5 Hz finite impulse response bandpass filter. 
III. RESULT & DISCUSSION 
We assumed that PPG amplitude (PPGA) reflects blood 
volume and that dPPGA/PPGA is proportionally changed by 
strain. Based on these assumptions, we defined a PPG-based 
distensibility, PPGDa, with a following equation: 
(dPPGA/PPGA)/dP. Figure 1 shows the proposed PPGDa 
curve that changes with BP. Thin lines mean a rest state 
PPGDa, and thick lines are PPGDa after VM. A, the inflection 
point of BP waveform in systolic phase , moved to A' as BP 
increase, which means that more pressure is needed for the 
same blood volume increase. B, the inflection point of BP 
waveform in diastolic phase , is also moved to B’ as BP 
increase, which indicates that more pressure reduction is 
needed for the same blood volume decrease. These changes 
could be interpreted as a decrease of Da. 
In this study, we confirmed the possibility of drawing a 
distensibility-like curve by using BPc and PPG. This method 
can be used in various blood pressure studies including 
PTT-based blood pressure estimation after increasing the 
subjects and generalizing them. 
REFERENCES

[2] Folkow, Bjorn, G. Griyby, and O. Thulesius. "Adaptive structural 
changes of the vascular walls in hypertension and their relation to the 
control of the peripheral resistance." Acta physiologica scandinavica
